name: monday.com
summary: Work management platform with boards, automations and views — plus separately-priced CRM, Dev and Service products.
best_for: teams who want one visual system for projects and work, and who will actually use the automations and views that justify the per-seat price at Standard or above
skip_if: you are two or three people who need a shared list. The free tier caps at 2 seats and 3 boards, and paying per seat for views you will not use is the most common way this gets expensive. Also skip it if you only want the CRM, since that is a separate subscription and worth pricing against dedicated CRMs
honest_knock: The seat price is not the product price. monday sells four products — Work Management, CRM, Dev and Service — each on its own subscription, and the $9 you see first is the cheapest tier of one of them. A sales team that wants the CRM is buying a second subscription on top of whatever Work Management costs, with a three-seat minimum of its own. The second number to find before you commit is the automation cap. Standard allows 250 automation actions a month across the whole account. If you are buying monday because of the automations you saw demoed, 250 is roughly one workflow running a few times a day — and the next step up is Pro at $19 a seat against Standard's $12. Free is capped at two seats and three boards, which makes it a preview rather than a plan.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-08-26 on monday.com/pricing over a US connection, at their default of 10 seats on yearly billing; re-read 2026-09-29 in a rendered browser from a Dutch connection, where the page serves euros with the same numerals on all three paid tiers and the AI-credit line with its equal 'special monthly discount' is unchanged) Free covers two seats. Basic is $9 per seat a month, a total of $90; Standard $12, down from $14, for $120 instead of $140; Pro $19, down from $22, for $190 instead of $220. Enterprise is quoted. The seat count is the thing to watch: the per-seat figure moves with team size, so a price read at ten seats is not what three or fifty will cost. Yearly billing is marked as 18% off, and each paid tier carries its own monthly AI-credit allowance rather than selling AI separately.
